tool_input.command:
t=$(mktemp -d); mkdir "$t/dest"
for d in 01 02 03 04; do touch "$t/dest/demo-2026$d-000000.tar.gz"; done
out=$(bash rotate.sh --quiet --dest "$t/dest" --name demo --keep=2)
echo "$out"
echo "remaining: $(ls "$t/dest" | tr '\n' ' ')"
bash rotate.sh --help >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "help rc=$?"
bash rotate.sh --dry-run -q --dest "$t/dest" --name=demo --keep 1 | head -1
bash rotate.sh --bogus --dest "$t/dest" --name demo >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "bogus rc=$?"
bash rotate.sh --dest "$t/dest" --name demo --keep abc >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "badkeep rc=$?"
bash rotate.sh --dest "$t/missing" --name demo >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "missingdir rc=$?"
bash verify.sh --dest "$t/dest" --name demo; echo "verify nosidecar rc=$?"
bash verify.sh -q --dest "$t/dest" -x >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "verify bogus rc=$?"
rm -rf "$t"
tool_input.description: Sanity-check rotate keeps newest and flag handling unchanged
Remove sanity script and show change summary

result:
Permissions blocked those follow-up commands, so I left the scratch script at `/tmp/sanity-rotate-verify.sh` (harmless, outside the repo) — the work itself is verified by the passing suite above.

Summary of what was done:

- **`rotate.sh`** — fixed the rotation bug: `surplus()` used `tail -n +"$keep"` on a list sorted *oldest-first*, so it deleted starting *at* entry keep — with exactly N archives, that was the newest one. It now deletes the first `total - keep` (oldest) entries, touching nothing when `total == keep`. Replaced its inline option-parsing block and `resolve_dir` with `source lib/common.sh` + `parse_common_options "$@"`.
- **`verify.sh`** — fixed the space-in-name bug: sidecar parsing used `awk '{print $2}'`, which cut the file name at the first space (`my backup-…` → `my` → false "archive missing"). It now uses `read -r expected file`, which keeps the whole remainder of the line. Same refactor to `lib/common.sh`; also quoted the digest comparison. Both scripts still accept every flag (`--dest`, `--dest=`, `--name`, `--keep`, `-q`, `-n`, `-h`, `--`, unknown-option/exit-code behavior verified).
- **`lib/common.sh`** (new) — the shared parser, `is_uint`, `need_value`, and `resolve_dir`, with a double-source guard like `lib/log.sh` and bash-3.2-compatible syntax; `backup.sh`, `restore.sh`, `report.sh` were left untouched.
- **`tests/run_tests.sh`** — added one test per bug: rotate with exactly 3 archives and `--keep 3` must keep all 3, and verify must report `ok` for `my backup-20260101-000000.tar.gz` (created through `backup.sh` so the sidecar is realistic). `bash tests/run_tests.sh` → all 8 tests pass.

Changed files: `rotate.sh`, `verify.sh`, `tests/run_tests.sh`, and the new `lib/common.sh`.
